If you like point-and-klick adventures and/or pixel art games, please buy [i]The Slaughter[/i] Act I. At a discount, full price… both should support the one-man developer team. 

Yes, it might be that after 10 years we might never get an Act II but maybe if more people buy it (and review it) the developer will finish it. 

Ef not, I think you still will have around 3 hours of good entertaining fun in a great atmosphere and writing. Also, the developer placed some things in the perspective so that they seem to stand at the edge of the screen where you look “in” which I have never seen before and is kind of neat – and very well done. 

Yes, the baseline of the story as of the [i]The Slaughter[/i] as far as we get to see it in Act I has been told before: A murderer called “The ripper” kills prostitutes in London in the 1880s. You are an out of luck private investigator who gets dragged into the case… but the story told in a fresh way, the character interesting and sympathetic and the dialogue is exellent.

So, please give it a try. I think you will enjoy it. 

Only thing that irritated is something about the movement of the protagonist… I am not sure but as far as I can say, I think his arms are animated too short… which is kind of funny.

This is a mixed review.

Cons: This game has fallen into the classic, modern retro-adventure game trap, by which I mean the puzzles are far too easy and its almost a walking simulator where you just click to advance. There is only one puzzle I can recall that has even a molecule of critical thinking involved (one involving a clamp). I have no idea why developers think the clientele for these sort of games is so dumb. What could have been a great game is turned into a 5/10 or so because there is literally nothing to think about. It's also a fairly short game, and it has no voice acting - although these two factors are more excusable, in my opinion, than the lack of thinking needed to finish the game.

Pros: The Victorian London setting is beautiful as always - such a classic setting for adventure games. The music is also quite haunting and charming, which took me by surprise a few times (especially the very last scene of the game before the credits roll has some really nice piano music). The dialogue is quite good too, some witty humor, some good historical nods etc.

Сюжет: играем за частного детектива по-имени Сидни Эмерсон и сначала решаем проблему с поиском потерянной собачки, а затем расследуем убийство девушки Элис Фэирчайлд - одной из жертв Потрошителя.
По игровому процессу: это квест, практически старой школы, но тут всего два выбора, что можно делать мышкой - осмотреть или испольковать предмет каким-либо образом. Есть головоломки, мини-игры, однако за провал игра никак не накажет, так что проиграть в целом очень трудно. В каких-то моментах можно потупить, но если не взять какую-то вещь. Единственное, что может выбесить - мини-игра в пабе, где нужно попасть монетками между двух линий. Час, наверное, сидела. А ещё там нельзя сохраняться в самом процессе - проиграешь автоматом и обзовут читером) Мне понравился главный герой - не дурак и весьма забавен. В целом, мне понравились все персонажи. По поводу истории в целом: она клишированная. Но в данном случае для меня это не минус, так как точно кто убийца не знаем, но у меня есть персонаж под подозрением. Кстати, тут есть и сосед, зазывающий Сидни в гости на бокал крепкого и подглядывающий за главным героем через дырочку в ванной, также есть момент с переодеванием в мадаму. Хотелось бы музыкального сопровождения побольше, но делаю скидку на то, что у разраба вряд ли был большой бюджет.
Из минусов, как ни странно, назову только пиксель-арт. Нет, он выполнен нормально, но тут лично мне бы хотелось, чтобы была анимационная рисовка - перснажи были бы более "читабельны" что ли. А так можно просто пофантазировать, хотя в диалогах можно было бы добавить лица персонажей как в Shadow of the Comet. И нет озвучки, так что тоже включаем воображение. BottomLine at the Top:  A "high def, low res" retro pixel art mystery horror game with an intriguing 19th century murder mystery story.  Act one of a three act game the subsequent acts are, as of this writing, in development limbo.  Still an excellent game for the P&C aficionado who appreciates a well-crafted adventure game experience.   


Pros
-------------------------------------
-Aesthetic design is a stylistic blend of retro pixel graphics on a modern engine that allows for lighting and depth effects.  Use of the depth effects is something I haven’t seen used like in this game before with lots of zooming in and out.  It provides for a more dynamic feel to the game like you’re watching a movie.  This has some of the most impressive animations in a retro style game that I've seen of late.
-Good intro that gets you interested in the story.
-A couple of the cutscenes are just fantastic.  Also has some fun surrealist dream sequences.  Overall, its real cinema quality story telling.
-Has autosaves. 
-Built in hint system and journal that keeps track of progress that provides a reminder of where you were in the game if you haven’t played in a while.
-High quality music and sound effects.
-Has one minigame that features a skip function.


Meh.
-------------------------------------
-No voices.  This isn’t always a bad thing and its usually a design choice.  For this game I think having voices would have worked out as a positive.  
-Puzzles are not especially challenging.  Except for a few times where I got stuck, they primarily exist to move the story along.  It’s still not a visual novel, but it does get borderline there at some points.  
-Load game screen takes a couple of seconds to show used saved game slots, during which it shows all slots as empty and gives me a small heart attack.
-Sprite walking routine is a little rigid.
-Some minor pixel hunting
-There is some unintuitive event scripting where it’s not obvious that you must do one action before your able to do another (gambling against the drunkard requires looking at him first before being able to place a wager)
  

Cons
-------------------------------------
-Alt-F12 opens a developer tools window.  Not only does this not allow for screenshot taking but it seems like a sloppy thing to leave in a finished game.
-No double click fast movement.  Double click fast travel to next location only works occasionally.


People are invariably going to compare this to a game of similar style, "The Last Door".  It turns out that retro pixel graphics as a medium is great for horror type games.  They are both excellent games and I don't think that one "wins" over the other as some of the other reviews have stated.  All I know is that the quality of this game should not be judged on the fact that its other acts have yet to be released (and may never be released).  It is still an excellent game that yes does leave you on a cliff hanger.  The developer has stated that it did not sell as well as was hoped but he is hoping to release future acts after he completes another large project he is working on.  At $6 regular asking price for approx. 2.5 hours of gameplay it is a little steep for an "unfinished" p&c game.  If you are a big p&c aficionado, can pick this up on sale, and understand that it was designed as the first act in a 3-part series, then I would say pick it up and try it out!

[h1]Sherlock Holmes für Arme[/h1]

Spätes [b]19. Jahrhundert[/b]. [b]London[/b]. [b]Detektivgeschichte[/b]

Vorab: Da es der Erste Teil einer Geschichte sein soll, betrachte ich das Spiel als Teil eines größeren Ganzen.

The Slaughter ist ein kleines Point-and-Klick Indi mit feiner Pixelgrafik. Es erinnert vom Rahmen her stark an Sherlock Holmes plus eine Prise Inception.
Hört sich nach einer schönen Idee an, ist aber an vielen Stellen noch nicht ideal umgesetzt, genrebedingt zieht sich das Gameplay stellenweise sehr und das Salz in der Suppe schmeckt irgendwie noch nach Pfeffer.

Dazu hab ich persönlich Probleme gehabt mit der englischen Fassung, die für ein Spiel ungewöhnlich viele Fremdwörter enthält, wodurch ich nicht immer alles verstanden habe und Google Übersetzer rechts aufm Laptop ging auf Dauer auf die Nerven und war nicht schnell genug im Verhältnis zum verschwindend schnellen Text.
Dennoch war's mir das irgendwie alles wert, denn The Slaughter liefert gleichzeitig doch eine schön kreative Geschichte ab, gefüttert mit lustigen Dialogen.

[b]Kleiner Krimi[/b]
Nicht nur der Rahmen, sondern auch der Inhalt erinnert an Sherlock Holmes; und zwar das Spiel [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/241260/Sherlock_Holmes_Crimes_and_Punishments/]Crimes and Punishments[/url]. Aber wie gesagt, alles klein gehalten und im Pixelstyle. Es kam mir stellenweise fast so vor, als würde ich das Spiel weiterspielen, mit starkem Grafik Downgrade, kein Witz. Wer den etwas bekannteren Titel nicht kennt, der hört jetzt einfach mal ganz genau hin.

Zeugenbefragung, mit Objekten von Tatorten arbeiten, ein bisschen Lektüre und im trauten Heim die Puzzelteile zusammenfügen. Beide Spiele macht das aus, nur mag ich die begleitende Geschichte in Slaughter mehr, denn in Crimes and Punishments liegt der Fokus auf den Fällen. Da hat's Slaughter so wie in vielen Aspekten aber einfacher, weil es nur um einen Fall geht: [spoiler]Jack the Ripper[/spoiler].

Bei Movement und Umfang macht es keinen Sinn, zu vergleichen, da ist The Slaughter deutlich begrenzter. Keine Sprecherstimmen und auch kein freies Gehen. Die Atmosphäre ist deutlich angespannt und verkrampft. Das Lösen der wenigen Rätsel ist mit Sicherheit keine Kunst und würde bei hoher Frequenz schnell öde. Zum Glück übertreibt man es nicht und schafft es somit, dass 1, 2 Highlight Momente die klassischen Sammelaufgaben überdecken. 
Als kleines Gimmick und Abwechslung gibt es außerdem ein kleines britisches Pub-Game, was Spaß machen kann, wenn man Zielwasser getrunken hat, andernfalls den Kopf zerbricht.

[b]Empfehlung mit ein paar Abstrichen[/b]
Wer Pixel mag, eine schöne Geschichte oder Detektivspiele, dem empfehle ich das Spiel mal ganz vorsichtig. Aber auch nur im Sale, der Preis ist deutlich zu hoch.
Alle anderen sollten lieber die Finger davon lassen. Gegen Ende war ich auch eher froh als traurig, dass es vorbei war.

So as interesting as it was, it became just a pointless time-waster.

I streamed this game for I Need Diverse Games. The community was really taken by the storyline. I loved the setting, and also how the game leaves you wanting to know more! I can't wait until the next Act gets funded!

Awesome game. I hope that they are able to finish and release the other acts in the future. I felt that everything about this game was solid: pixel art graphics, sound, user interface, writing, etc. Definitely one of the better point & click games that I've played lately.

This is a relatively short (~2.5 hours), melancholy, gripping adventure game in the style of LucasArts or Sierra. The puzzling is the usual inventory-based kind, and minimal, so it's more of a visual novel than a true adventure. The graphics are the old-style pixel, and the music is quite good. Overall they promote the dreary Victorian atmosphere very well. The game's greatest strength is in its writing and characters.

I'm sorry to hear that the sales didn't go well enough to fund Act 2 and 3 immediately. When they come out they will definitely be on my radar.

I'm glad to see point and click adventure games are starting to make a comeback, I've missed them so much!

Now, this game:
I enjoyed it a lot!  The atmosphere, the storyline, the background music, the pixel art - all of it.

I only had 2 issues with this game:
1) the puzzles are a little too easy, IMO.  The only reason I have 6 hours in was because I left my PC on when we went to run errands and grab food (and we were gone for around 3 hours...so....yeah)
2) There is no way to make your character run, or speed up his movement.

So, is it worth a pickup?  If you can catch it on sale, absolutely!  Even if it isn't on sale...6.99 is like a fast food meal or a couple coffee drinks for 2.5-3.5 hours of gameplay with an interesting story....I WILL warn you though - the ending is a cliffhanger and if that sort of thing makes you crazy just get it on sale.

ps
And, I have Windows 10 and had no issues with playing this game.
I love this game, even if it is quite short and the puzzles are not too hard, it has an atmosphere which sucks me in everytime. I cannot wait for Act 2!

This is a fantastic third person point and click adventure from an independent producer. I thoroughly hope that the subsequent chapters get released.

The game is set in Victorian London when Jack the Ripper was at work. The gameplay focuses on learning things through conversation and object based puzzles. The puzzles are well designed and logical but there is a bit of pixel hunting. The pixel hunting is the only thing that annoyed me in the game.

What really makes this game stand out is the quality of the script. It's appropriately dark at times but also has several lighter scenes which include a great sense of humour. The effort that has gone into the descriptions of surroundings is very rare, The sheer wit of the writer is  brilliant.

I'm looking forward to the next chapter(s).

Delightful point and click adventure, manages to feel classic and modern at the same time.
Great art, interesting setting and puzzles of exactly the right difficulty.
Oh, and awesome dream sequences - they deserve to be mentioned separately.

This is a mixed bag. The story is well told, but not that original (there might be more orginality hidden behind the dream stuff, but this remains to be unveiled yet).
The game itself it quite short (I've idled ingame), and the puzzles aren't really fun: some pixel hunting, some fetch-quests and some obtuse random stuff. The game feels unresponsive and clunky: the character walks quite slowly and has some pathfinding issues. Since he persists to walk to a hotspot when ever I want to try to apply an item there (just to tell me it won't work once he's arrived), solving puzzles feels sluggish and annoying sometimes.
The graphics are okay but not really a joy to watch, especially not the mainchars moonwalking. They serve their purpose nevertheless.
But, as said before, the narration is well done. For 8 € I'd expect more than a trailer ending with a cliffhanger, but nevertheless this game has much potential. Slightly recommanded in hope for a more polished second part.

As someone who plays point&click games for its story, I quite enjoyed this game. The puzzles are adequately challenging for fans of point&click genre. I felt the art and the sound are used to create a convincing Victorian atmosphere.

And the length is also fine for its price. I have been waiting a while for act two. I hope the developer gets around to it.

The game was not too good and not too bad. Something you can play, but you do not have to.

Really tidy game by a talented indie developer. Acts 2 and 3 are promised, really hope they can be released soon, and this will be expedited if gamers commit to buying the full season.

PROS:
- not too difficult, you shouldn't be getting stuck
- still enough story/atmosphere to entertain more experienced gamers
- nice, subtle humour
- unpretentious, retro-style graphics
- decent amount of game play, I imagine about 8-10 hours once all three acts are available, if you want to play thoroughly like a true point and click fan should!
- simple game physics in which very little can go wrong bug-wise (I have only really seen one glitch)
- just the right amount of dialogue
- rich story based on one of the more fascinating mysteries in the real world

CONS:
- okay, puzzles could be a bit more challenging

I've owned this game for almost 2 months and still haven't finished it.  The Slaughter started off very strong.  Witty dialog is off the charts; great characterization.  Interesting side characters and situations.  Graphics are ok.  Not the best pixel art, but it gets the job done.  I got stuck maybe once initially and I think I had to resort to the hint system, but after that the game went well.

Until it stopped being a point and click adventure and served up a mini-game.  I knew something was up, the story stalled, there was no direction, I ended up at the right location only out of a process of elimination.  And I ended up at the mini-game only because there was nothing else to do (still haven't a clue why my character is playing though).  The mini-game is half-penny where you are supposed to slide half-pennies across a board to certain distances.  It's mind numbingly boring.  Pong is more interesting and I hate those types of games.  But you either have to win, or play 3 rounds (last I heard) to progress.  Honestly, I'd rather do housework.  So, I have a clean house, but haven't finished this episode, and will probably never bother with another one.  Sad, really, this looked like a delightfully entertaining game.  And it was, until it wasn't.

I tried to get myself to refund the game, but the writing was so good that I put it off.  Now it's too late.  Perhaps I'll try to suffer past the half-penny game some day.  Maybe I'll make my own mini-game out of it:  buy some beer and take a drink every time I don't get a half-penny in a column.  Maybe that will get me through 3 rounds.  And afterwards I'll actually feel like the main character to boot!  Alas, there are so many other good games to play.  

TL;DR:  Great writing, ok graphics.  Story screeches to a dead halt with an tortuous mini-game that comes out of nowhere and doesn't appear to serve any purpose since there is no context to why you are wasting your time with it.  If you can get this at a steep sale....have you tried hidden object games?  Some of those are actually a lot of fun, and cheap too.
The mini-game is a bit pointless and annoying, but overall one of the better indie adventures. Looking forward to act two.
